title: Timing control: CreER and tamoxifen
objective: Explain how CreER + tamoxifen restricts recombination in time, and how tamoxifen dose controls how many cells are labeled (sparse labeling).

steps.title: Why plain Cre isn't enough
steps.body: Plain [[Cre]] fires whenever the driver gene is on — including during development, labeling more cells than you want (the gotcha from last lesson). You often want to choose **when** recombination happens. That's what **[[CreER]]** is for.

steps.title: How CreER works
steps.body: **CreER** fuses Cre to a modified estrogen receptor that traps it **inert in the cytoplasm**. It does nothing until you give **[[tamoxifen]]**, which lets CreER enter the nucleus for a short window and recombine. No tamoxifen → no recombination. (You'll see `CreER` and `CreERT2`; CreERT2 is just an improved version.)

visual.alt: CreER sits inert in the cytoplasm until tamoxifen is added, then enters the nucleus and recombines the DNA to switch the gene on.
visual.caption: No tamoxifen → CreER stays out · + tamoxifen → it enters the nucleus and recombines.

steps.prompt: You want to label a marker's cells in the ADULT and avoid developmental expression. What do you do?
options: Use plain Cre and accept whatever it happens to label
Use CreER and give tamoxifen only in adulthood
Use a brighter reporter to pick out the adult cells
Inject the reporter protein directly into the tissue
steps.explanation: CreER + adult tamoxifen opens the recombination window only when you choose, so cells that expressed the gene only during development aren't captured.

variants.setup: You want to label a marker's cells in the adult and avoid developmental expression.

Use CreER and give tamoxifen only in adulthood

variants.reveal: CreER stays inactive until tamoxifen, so dosing adults captures adult expression and skips the developmental lineage.

steps.title: The dose trick: sparse labeling
steps.body: Tamoxifen dose controls **how many** cells recombine. A **low** dose recombines only a few scattered cells — letting you trace **single neurons** and their endings without a tangle of overlapping labels. This is exactly how the colon paper traced individual [[DRG]] afferent endings (counting wrappings per ending). More tamoxifen → more cells; less → sparser.

visual.alt: Interactive: a slider sets tamoxifen dose; a field of DRG neurons goes from a few labeled cells (sparse, traceable) to most labeled (dense, overlapping).
visual.caption: Drag the dose: sparse (traceable) → dense (overlapping).

steps.setup: You want to measure the branching of individual Bmpr1b+ colon afferent endings. You have a Bmpr1b-CreER; [[reporter]] mouse.
options: A high dose of tamoxifen to label essentially everything
A low dose so that only a few isolated neurons are labeled
No tamoxifen at all, relying on background recombination
Tamoxifen given only during embryonic development
steps.reveal: Low-dose tamoxifen gives sparse, isolated labeling — so each traced ending clearly belongs to one neuron. High-dose would label so many that endings overlap and single-cell morphology is unmeasurable.

variants.prompt: You want to measure the branching of individual labeled afferent endings. What tamoxifen strategy fits?

A low dose so that only a few isolated neurons are labeled
No tamoxifen at all, relying on background recombination
Tamoxifen given only during embryonic development
variants.explanation: Low-dose tamoxifen gives sparse, mosaic recombination — ideal for resolving single neurons.

sources.citation: Wolfson RL, et al. DRG afferents that mediate physiologic and pathologic mechanosensation from the distal colon. Cell 186:3368-3385 (2023).
sources.note: Used low-dose-tamoxifen sparse CreER labeling to trace single afferent endings.
